question: When the pH value of soils is more than 7.5, they are considered to be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**alkaline soils**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Soils with a pH value greater than 7.5 are classified as **alkaline soils**.
 
• Alkaline soils typically contain a high concentration of **calcium carbonate (lime)**, which raises the pH level.
 
• Such soils may exhibit poor fertility due to the reduced availability of essential nutrients like iron, manganese, and phosphorus at higher pH levels.
 
• These soils are commonly found in **arid and semi-arid regions** where evaporation exceeds precipitation, leading to salt accumulation.
 
• The correction of alkaline soils often involves adding **organic matter, sulfur compounds, or gypsum** to lower the pH and improve soil structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil pH**: A measure of the acidity or alkalinity of the soil, ranging from 0 (highly acidic) to 14 (highly alkaline), with 7 being neutral.
 
• **Acidic Soils**: Soils with a pH below 7, often found in regions with high rainfall, as leaching removes basic cations.
 
• **Neutral Soils**: Soils with a pH around 7, which are considered ideal for most agricultural crops.
 
• **Effects of High pH**: Alkaline soils can lead to deficiencies of micronutrients like zinc, iron, and copper, which are essential for plant growth.
 
• **Soil Correction**: Techniques like adding elemental sulfur, acid-forming fertilizers, or organic amendments can help lower soil pH and enhance its fertility.
